scenes.title: Greater Wrongs
scenes.summary: A wrong is greater the greater the injustice it comes from, so the smallest can be the greatest, as Callistratus argued against Melanopus over three sacred half-obols; greater too is a wrong with no adequate punishment or remedy, or one for which the victim punished himself, as Sophocles argued for Euctemon.

scenes.title: More Marks of a Greater Wrong
scenes.summary: Wrongs done alone or first, repeated, or the cause of new laws and prisons, as in Argos; brutal, premeditated or more fearful than pitiable; breaking oaths and pledges; committed in court by false witnesses; shameful; against benefactors; and against the unwritten law, or, in another way, the written.
